rulings.challenge_claim: The row's two supporting textual claims for the 4:20 opening -- the bni-opening ordinal and the unbroken-imperative-mood argument -- are both byte-false.
rulings.grounds: Split claim, byte-checked independently. (1) ORDINAL, REFUTED as framed: the inventory's own count_object for bni_address is "verses containing the word-bound vocative token beni, any position" (prov_device_inventory.json), i.e. an occurrence-in-span count -- that yields 5 in Prov.3.1-4.27 (3.1, 3.11, 3.21, 4.10, 4.20), which is the object LF counted. But the row's own sentence asserts a different object: "the part's fourth and final bni-OPENING" -- a row/unit-opening count, not a raw occurrence count. Independently re-derived from writer/p02_rows.jsonl (11 rows, Prov.3.1-4.27) cross-referenced against the inventory: only 4 of those 11 rows open on their own first verse containing beni -- P02-001 Prov.3.1 (בְּ֭נִי, verse-initial), P02-004 Prov.3.21 (בְּ֭נִי, verse-initial), P02-009 Prov.4.10 (בְּ֭נִי, second word), P02-011 Prov.4.20 (בְּ֭נִי, verse-initial). Prov.3.11's beni (בְּנִ֣י, third word of oshb:Prov.3.11) falls mid-span inside row P02-002 (Prov.3.5-3.12), which itself opens at 3.5, not 3.11 -- so 3.11 is not a row-opening. Under the object the row's own sentence names, "fourth and final" is digit-correct; LF's challenge counted the wrong object (see the companion OL ruling on this row for the register defect the ordinal phrasing does carry). (2) IMPERATIVE-MOOD CONTINUITY, UPHELD: oshb:Prov.4.22 reads "כִּֽי חַיִּ֣ים הֵ֭ם לְמֹצְאֵיהֶ֑ם וּֽלְכָל בְּשָׂר֥וֹ מַרְפֵּֽא" -- a third-person ki-motive clause with 3mp/3ms suffixes (lemotz'eihem, bes'aro) and no 2ms suffix or imperative verb, unlike every other verse in the span (4.20-21, 4.23-27 all carry 2ms suffixes -kha/-ekha or imperative forms; web:Prov.4.22 “For they are life to those who find them, and health to their whole body.”). So the rejected_alternative's claim that "the second-person addressee and imperative mood carry unbroken from 4.20 through 4.27" is inaccurate: 4.22 is the one verse in the span that breaks it.
rulings.remedy: Correct rejected_alternative's continuity clause: replace "the second-person addressee and imperative mood carry unbroken from 4.20 through 4.27" with a claim that survives 4.22 -- e.g. argue 4.22 functions as a subordinate ki-motive clause grounding 4.20-21's imperatives rather than breaking the unit's cohesion, or drop the unbroken-continuity claim and rest the rejection on the single-organ progression (heart/mouth/eyes/feet) already argued in rationale/device_notes. Test: every verse cited in a claimed unbroken person/mood run must be spot-checked in verse_map_oshb.json for the claimed person markers before the claim ships -- this is the check that caught the original error. Leave the "fourth and final bni-opening" ordinal phrase's digit alone (it is correct); its register problem is a separate defect (see OL ruling, this row).

rulings.challenge_claim: The phrase "the part's fourth and final bni-opening" counts against the writer's own mechanical part-tiling rather than a textual unit -- file-order/production talk barred from row prose.
rulings.grounds: Independently re-derived: "the part" cannot resolve to parent_collection C1 (Prov.1.1-9.18) -- bni_address recurs at Prov.1.8/1.10/1.15/2.1 before 3.1 (prov_device_inventory.json refs), so a collection-wide row-opening count would exceed four well before reaching 4.20. It resolves only to writer_part p02 (Prov.3.1-4.27, 11 rows per writer/p02_rows.jsonl), a campaign scratch-tiling artifact, where the row-opening count is exactly 4 (see ruling on the LF item, this row, for the independent re-derivation). book_strategy Prov.md Sec.8 and TOOLKIT.md's Standing rules both bar "positional row references" and "file-order talk...in row prose EVER"; using the writer_part boundary as the counting frame for an ordinal claim in row prose is exactly that, independent of whether the resulting digit is accurate.
rulings.remedy: Strike the ordinal claim rather than reword it: checked against C1 and against the chs.1-7 bni distribution as candidate literary scopes, "fourth and final" has no true non-tiling literary referent, so no rewording preserves both truth and register. Replace "the part's fourth and final bni-opening" with a plain, scope-free description, e.g. a statement that 4.20 reopens the singular beni address recurring earlier at 3.1, 3.21, and 4.10 (verse-anchored, no ordinal, no part/file noun). Test: re-read against book_strategy Prov.md Sec.8's REGISTER PURGE list; the cure must not reintroduce any writer_part/file-tiling reference into row prose.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row's own back seam (5:19/5:20) carries an undisclosed byte-true catchword -- the verb-root shagah repeated verbatim across the boundary.
rulings.grounds: Byte-verified: oshb:Prov.5.19 closes "תִּשְׁגֶּ֥ה תָמִֽיד" and oshb:Prov.5.20's second word is "תִשְׁגֶּ֣ה" -- the same root (shagah, "be captivated/go astray"), and WEB preserves the pun at both sites ("captivated"/"captivated"), so this is not a translation-only artifact. A genuine, disclosure-worthy device straddling this row's own back seam per TOOLKIT.md's cross-seam-cohesion rule. CONVERGENCE: the same device is also raised, from the other side of the identical seam, against the neighboring row P03-004 by both LF and OL (see those rulings). This is ONE seam-pair device, not a defect unique to this row -- ruled here as the P03-003-side half of a single coordinated disclosure fix, per the standing rule that seam-pair cures are one edit. It does not reopen the register-shift boundary the row argues (blessing/imperative vs. rhetorical question).
rulings.remedy: Add one clause to P03-003's device_notes disclosing that the closing verb (root shagah, oshb:Prov.5.19) recurs verbatim as the opening verb of the following row's rhetorical question (oshb:Prov.5.20), consistent with -- not overturning -- the register-shift boundary already argued. Issue together with the matching P03-004 front-seam clause (see that ruling) as ONE coordinated seam-pair edit, not two independent patches. Test: both clauses must name the same device (root shagah, oshb:Prov.5.19/5.20) and must not re-argue or alter either row's span/unit_type -- disclosure only.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row's own front seam (5:19/5:20) shares the identical undisclosed shagah catchword with the preceding row, and the row also misses that the same root closes its own span at 5:23, forming an inclusio it never names.
rulings.grounds: Two distinct sub-claims, both byte-confirmed. (i) FRONT-SEAM CATCHWORD: same device as the P03-003 ruling above -- oshb:Prov.5.19 closes "תִּשְׁגֶּ֥ה תָמִֽיד", oshb:Prov.5.20 opens its rhetorical question with "תִשְׁגֶּ֣ה" as the second word. This is the SAME seam-pair device already ruled on P03-003, not a second, independent defect -- CONVERGENT, one coordinated cure spanning both rows. (ii) INTERNAL INCLUSIO: a genuinely separate, row-internal finding -- oshb:Prov.5.20's "תִשְׁגֶּ֣ה" and oshb:Prov.5.23's closing "יִשְׁגֶּֽה" are both shagah-root forms bracketing this row's own four verses (5.20-5.23), an inclusio nowhere named in device_notes (which covers only the 5.23 petuchah and parallelism texture). This is independent of the front-seam disclosure gap: it is a claim about this row's OWN internal structure, not about continuity across a boundary, so it is a distinct defect from (i), not a duplicate of it.
rulings.remedy: (i) See the coordinated P03-003/P03-004 seam-pair cure in the P03-003 ruling above -- add the matching front-seam clause to this row's device_notes as one half of that single edit. (ii) Separately, add an explicit inclusio note to this row's own device_notes: the root shagah opens (oshb:Prov.5.20) and closes (oshb:Prov.5.23) the row's own span, framing its question-to-consequence argument -- additive disclosure only, no boundary or unit_type change. Test: the inclusio clause must name both verse refs and the shared root, and the edit must not alter this row's span or unit_type.

rulings.challenge_claim: The 5.20-5.23 boundary argument omits a paseq inside its own span (Prov.5.21) and does not disclose a root-level wordplay tying its opening verb back across the seam it calls a "reopening."
rulings.grounds: Two sub-claims, both byte-confirmed as real, but the bundled HIGH severity is corrected downward: neither sub-claim touches the row's boundary/unit_type call, both are pure disclosure-symmetry gaps, which this cluster otherwise treats as medium (cf. the LF ordinal/continuity item on P02-011). (i) PASEQ, a THIRD, DISTINCT defect (unrelated to the shagah root): pmarks_Prov.json's paseq table carries an entry for Prov.5.21 (count 1), a mark inside this row's own Prov.5.20-5.23 span that is absent from boundary_evidence_refs and device_notes, even though this cluster's rows consistently disclose in-span paseq presence elsewhere (P03-005 discloses its 6.3 paseq; P03-006 discloses 6.9 and 6.10; P03-007 discloses 6.14) -- P03-004 breaks that established disclosure-symmetry convention. (ii) SHAGAH ROOT: byte-confirmed (oshb:Prov.5.20 "תִשְׁגֶּ֣ה", oshb:Prov.5.23 "יִשְׁגֶּֽה", and the preceding row's oshb:Prov.5.19 "תִּשְׁגֶּ֥ה תָמִֽיד") -- but this is CONVERGENT with the seam-pair device already ruled on the P03-003/P03-004 LF items above (front-seam half) plus the internal-inclusio half already ruled in the P03-004 LF item; it is not a fourth distinct defect, it is the same two devices reached independently by OL.
rulings.remedy: (i) Add to P03-004's device_notes, matching the cluster's own established paseq-disclosure phrasing (cf. P03-005/006/007): "A paseq seg is attested at Prov.5.21; the inventory tallies presence only, no intra-verse position is claimed." (ii) Covered by the coordinated seam-pair cure (P03-003/P03-004 LF rulings above) and the internal-inclusio cure (P03-004 LF ruling above) -- do not add a third, separate shagah disclosure. Test: re-run the mark-disclosure-symmetry check (check_marks.py) on P03-004 after the paseq clause is added to confirm every span-relevant mark is now disclosed.

rulings.challenge_claim: The rejected_alternative compares this admonition_unit to the book's wisdom_poem spans, an easily-dismissed strawman that skips the real live rival: whether the third-person ant illustration should split from the direct sluggard address that resumes at 6:9.
rulings.grounds: book_strategy Prov.md Sec.6 confines wisdom_poem to 1:20-33, 3:13-20(?), ch.8, ch.9 -- third-person hymnic personification poems. Comparing 6:6-11 (direct second-person imperative/interrogative admonition) against that category is not a genuine contest; confirmed as an easy dismissal, not the row's strongest rival. Independently re-verified from bytes: oshb:Prov.6.6 opens second-person imperative, oshb:Prov.6.7-6.8 shift to third person describing the ant, and oshb:Prov.6.9 returns to direct second-person interrogative address -- a genuine internal person-alternation the row's rejected_alternative never engages or argues around. This does not overturn the row's final span or unit_type: the direct-address frame at 6.6 and 6.9-6.11 plausibly still governs the whole unit with the third-person material as embedded illustration, but the row's own stated rejected_alternative fails to test the real candidate.
rulings.remedy: Replace the wisdom_poem comparison in rejected_alternative with the real live rival: whether 6.7-6.8's third-person ant description should split from the second-person frame at 6.6/6.9-6.11, rejected because the third-person material functions as embedded illustration inside one continuous second-person admonition (framed on both sides by direct address to the sluggard), not as an independent voice-shift seam. Test: the replacement sentence must name a competing span/reading a reasonable analyst could actually hold for this exact stretch, not an unrelated unit_type drawn from a different part of the book.

rulings.challenge_claim: The 6.6-6.11 rationale does not disclose that its own closing participle shares the root halak with the participle opening the following unit at 6.12, a byte-true device invisible in the WEB rendering the row's argument leans on.
rulings.grounds: Byte-verified: oshb:Prov.6.11's second word is "כִמְהַלֵּ֥ךְ" and oshb:Prov.6.12's fifth word (after the two-word nominal subject and its two-word apposition) is "ה֝וֹלֵ֗ךְ" -- both participles of the same root halak ("walk/go"), straddling this row's own back seam. Confirmed invisible in WEB: 6.11 renders "as a robber" and 6.12 renders "is he who walks" -- unlike the shagah pun at 5.19/5.20 (which WEB does preserve as "captivated"/"captivated"), this device is obscured in translation, so it could not have surfaced from the WEB-visible contrast (imperative/interrogative vs. third-person participial portrait) the row's own rationale leans on. A genuine, undisclosed cross-seam device per TOOLKIT.md's cross-seam-cohesion rule. Does not overturn the boundary: a root recurrence across a register-shift seam is common Hebrew wisdom style and is not by itself decisive against the address-mode shift already argued.
rulings.remedy: Add to P03-006's device_notes: the root halak recurs across the row's own back seam (כִמְהַלֵּ֥ךְ closing 6.11; ה֝וֹלֵ֗ךְ opening 6.12's participial chain) -- disclosed as a lexical link the WEB rendering ("robber"/"walks") obscures; does not reopen the boundary, which rests on the address-mode shift (second-person imperative/interrogative vs. third-person participial portrait) already argued. Test: confirm root identity against consonantal_index.json's skeleton tier, and confirm the added clause does not alter unit_type or span.
